incidents.vector: Unknown attack method; attackers left a message on the blockchain claiming to be white-hat researchers.
incidents.impact: $320 million worth of Bitcoin extracted from Blockstream's Liquid Network platform; network paused pending investigation. If confirmed malicious, it would be the largest crypto-heist of 2026.

incidents.victim: French notaries (500+ offices, ~7% of all French notary firms)
incidents.vector: Phishing to gain persistent network access, then silently modifying banking details in wire transfers over a four-year campaign targeting notary offices across France.
incidents.impact: More than €35 million stolen from over 500 notary offices; France's ANSSI spent two years quietly helping victims remediate; concerns raised about potential forgery of notarized legal documents.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering via fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA page installed LoremIpsumLoader malware, which deployed Rhysida ransomware across two Berlin ministries.
incidents.impact: 5.79 TB of data stolen from Berlin's urban development and transport ministries, then published after Berlin refused a $2 million ransom demand; exposed personal data of public employees and residents including bank information, correspondence, and identity documents. Breach occurred three weeks before the city's September 20 election.

incidents.victim: Enterprise and consumer browser users globally
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a type confusion vulnerability (CVE-2026-85046) in Google Chromium's V8 JavaScript engine.
incidents.impact: CISA added to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with confirmed active exploitation; federal agencies must remediate urgently under BOD 26-04.

incidents.victim: Thomson Reuters / Court systems in 12+ US states and Canada
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to C-Track, a court case management platform operated by a Thomson Reuters subsidiary; attackers maintained access from March through June 2026.
incidents.impact: Sealed court records, Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, and medical data exposed across courts in Alabama, Kentucky, Montana, Nevada, and at least eight other US states, plus Canadian courts. Some victims were notified months after discovery.

incidents.victim: Transportation and government agencies (Mexico, Ecuador); financial sector (Brazil)
incidents.vector: Living-off-the-land techniques combined with AI-assisted script generation via self-hosted LLM interfaces; job-themed phishing for initial access; SOCKS5 proxy tunneling for data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data exfiltrated from Mexican federal ministries and municipal water utilities, and Brazilian financial institutions; AI tools including commercial LLMs used to accelerate intrusion tradecraft throughout campaigns active since February 2026.

incidents.victim: Organizations using SonicWall SMA 1000 remote access gateways
incidents.vector: Chained exploitation of CVE-2026-83548 (pre-authentication SSRF, CVSS 10.0) and CVE-2026-83549 (OS command injection) enabling unauthenticated remote code execution on internet-facing edge devices.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed; CISA added both CVEs to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; SonicWall urges immediate patching and re-imaging of compromised devices. Fifth KEV addition to SMA 1000 since mid-December 2025.

incidents.vector: AI agents exploited a public API endpoint, then autonomously mapped the network, seized master credentials from secrets management, hijacked CI/CD pipelines, and repurposed the victim's own cloud AI endpoints as post-compromise infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Complete enterprise network compromise in under 10 hours using over 50 MITRE ATT&CK techniques; source code, cloud access keys, and root credentials stolen; attacker left an 80-page security audit of the victim's environment.

incidents.vector: Social engineering to compromise credentials and gain access to cloud-hosted third-party applications, enabling unauthorized data access and exfiltration over a four-day intrusion beginning August 21.
incidents.impact: Data stolen from oncology, surgical, and specialty business units; ShinyHunters demanded over $55 million ransom; McKesson distributes approximately one-third of all pharmaceuticals across North America. Customer data affected across multiple business units.

incidents.victim: IDScan.net (identity verification provider) and its clients
incidents.vector: Active breach of IDScan.net identity verification systems deployed at rental car agencies, marijuana dispensaries, hotels, and Fortune 500 clients; infrared and UV scans of IDs captured and exfiltrated continuously.
incidents.impact: 153 million+ US and Canadian driver's license scans now sold via dark web service 'Nexus,' including records of senior US government officials; FBI's New Orleans field office launched investigation; data actively harvested for over a year with 400,000 new records added per day.

incidents.victim: JetBrains (Cadence cloud LLM training platform and customers)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in JetBrains' own TeamCity CI/CD servers to pivot into the Cadence cloud-based LLM training platform.
incidents.impact: Source code and credentials stored by customers in Cadence platform instances likely stolen; customers advised that any sensitive data in Cadence may be at risk.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-82329 (CVSS 9.8), an authentication bypass in default JFrog Artifactory configurations enabling unauthenticated admin access with no user interaction required; public proof-of-concept published.
incidents.impact: Attackers minting administrator tokens and enumerating users, credentials, and federated access configurations; CISA added to KEV; JFrog Artifactory is used by 83% of Fortune 100 companies, making supply chain tampering a significant downstream risk.

incidents.victim: Organizations using PaperCut NG/MF print management software
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578 (both CVSS 8.8+) in internet-exposed PaperCut print management server interfaces.
incidents.impact: Multiple confirmed customer incidents; PaperCut is widely used by universities, corporations, and government agencies; historically exploited as initial access for ransomware operators including Clop and Bl00dy.

incidents.victim: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Unknown initial access; Qilin ransomware gang breached a standalone system within the federal law enforcement agency.
incidents.impact: System containing information about ATF investigation targets compromised; senior officials designated the breach a federal 'major incident'; potential exposure of confidential law enforcement investigation identities.

incidents.victim: Global software supply chain (thousands of businesses worldwide)
incidents.vector: Embedded malicious code in hundreds of open-source tools via stolen developer credentials from GitHub and NPM; the Shai-Hulud self-propagating worm enabled cyclical compromise of new developer environments and repositories.
incidents.impact: Described as the longest-running software supply chain attack spree on record; two suspects (ages 21 and 23) arrested in Western Australia by Australian Federal Police; thousands of global businesses compromised.

incidents.victim: European government and diplomatic organizations (Romania, Spain, Türkiye)
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures delivered HOOKEDGE batch-script backdoor; webhook services used for command-and-control, payload staging, and data exfiltration to blend with legitimate network traffic.
incidents.impact: Intelligence collection against European diplomatic targets linked to Moldovan political affairs and NATO-adjacent governance; campaign ran from September 2025 through at least April 2026 with continuous refinement to evade detection.

incidents.victim: US federal agencies (NASA, Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, HHS, NIH) and critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: QScan automated vulnerability scanner (200+ proof-of-concept exploits) combined with QTRouter IoT botnet to exploit edge device vulnerabilities in Ivanti, Fortinet, Citrix, F5, and BeyondTrust products, concealing attack origins through compromised third-party devices.
incidents.impact: Eight-year espionage operation targeting multiple US federal agencies and critical infrastructure; DOJ/FBI seized QScan and QTRouter platforms on August 26; group operated by Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company providing services to China's Ministry of State Security and PLA.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated RCE via improper sanitization of SNMP notification input in Zimbra (CVE-2026-73570); SNMP notifications are enabled by default in vulnerable versions.
incidents.impact: CISA issued a three-day remediation deadline for federal civilian agencies under BOD 26-04; active exploitation campaigns documented by Poland's CERT Polska since August 16; successful exploitation yields full control of email, calendar, and communications infrastructure.
